mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for the month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), manufacturing output contraction signals reduced corporate capacity utilization and lower future earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals stronger economic activity and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS has increased for at least 3 months, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 5.0% signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0% for the month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a labor market slowdown that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from prior month, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4.5%), the Federal Reserve's aggressive tightening of monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.
